title: Finite-free counit comparison on arbitrary sheaf topoi in specified coordinates
statement:
Let $h:\mathscr X\to\mathscr Y$ be a morphism of sheaf topoi on sites small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $a:R_Y\to S_Y$ be a map of commutative ring sheaves on $\mathscr Y$, put $R_X=h^{-1}R_Y$, $S_X=h^{-1}S_Y$, $a_X=h^{-1}a$, and use the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $L_R=h_R^*\dashv G_R=Rh_{*,R}$ and $L_S=h_S^*\dashv G_S=Rh_{*,S}$ be the adjunctions obtained by deriving the canonical module adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Write $E_T=S_T\otimes_{R_T}^{\mathbf L}-$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and $r_T$ for exact scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Fix $\theta_Y:R_Y^{\oplus d}\xrightarrow{\sim}r_YS_Y$, $d\geq0$ finite, and $\theta_X=h^{-1}\theta_Y$.
For $K\in D(R_X)$ let $\gamma_K:E_YG_RK\to G_SE_XK$ be the adjunct of the canonical pullback/tensor comparison $L_SE_YG_RK\cong E_XL_RG_RK$ followed by $E_X(\varepsilon_{R,K})$ [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. The canonical ordinary identity $r_Yh_{*,S}=h_{*,R}r_X$ induces an isomorphism $d:r_YG_S\xrightarrow{\sim}G_Rr_X$ respecting adjoint transposes. With the coordinate isomorphisms $\Phi_T$ of [lem-sfb-derived-finite-free-scalar-coordinates], one has
$$G_R(\Phi_{X,K})\circ d_{E_XK}\circ r_Y(\gamma_K)\circ\Phi_{Y,G_RK}^{-1}=\sigma_K:(G_RK)^{\oplus d}\longrightarrow G_R(K^{\oplus d}),$$
where $\sigma_K\iota_i=G_R(\iota_i)$. Its inverse is $\sum_i\iota_iG_R(p_i)$, with $\iota_i,p_i$ the finite biproduct inclusions and projections. In particular $\gamma_K$ is an isomorphism for every unbounded $K$, with no geometric or boundedness hypothesis.

proof.text: Write $H_R=h_{*,R}$ and $H_S=h_{*,S}$ for the ordinary functors. Scalar restriction $r_T$ is exact and is right adjoint to ordinary scalar extension. By the finite-free coordinate lemma that extension is exact for $T=X,Y$; the pulled-back frame is the specified $\theta_X$. The geometric inverse images $L_R,L_S$ are exact, since the structural coefficient maps are identities. Their ordinary adjunctions are the module adjunctions in the statement. There are canonical ordinary identifications $u:L_Rr_Y\cong r_XL_S$ and $c:r_YH_S\cong H_Rr_X$: both leave the underlying geometric sheaf operation unchanged, and the actions agree by $a_X=h^{-1}a$. The ordinary counits agree under these identifications: forgetting the coefficient action gives the same geometric evaluation $h^{-1}h_*N\to N$. Thus $r_X(\varepsilon^0_{S,N})=\varepsilon^0_{R,r_XN}$ after inserting $u$ and $c$.

The small-site module categories have unbounded K-injective resolutions. Apply the exact-left-adjoint criterion to scalar extension $\dashv r_X$: step 1 gives its exactness, so $r_X$ sends K-injectives to K-injectives. For an $S_X$-complex $J$ which is K-injective, both $r_YG_S(QJ)$ and $G_Rr_X(QJ)$ are therefore computed, respectively, by $Q(r_YH_SJ)$ and $Q(H_Rr_XJ)$; for the first, the exact functor $r_Y$ is computed termwise by its localization comparison. Define $d_{QJ}$ by $Q(c_J)$ through these computation isomorphisms. The Hom comparison for K-injectives represents every derived map by a unique homotopy class between K-injective representatives. Naturality of $c$ for those classes makes these components natural; changing representatives conjugates by the corresponding homotopy equivalences and gives the same components. Hence they define the canonical natural isomorphism $d:r_YG_S\cong G_Rr_X$, normalized by the ordinary identity on K-injectives. This constructs the required comparison on all unbounded objects.

Apply the exact-square derived-counit theorem with $F'=h_S^*$, $F=h_R^*$, $G'=H_S$, $G=H_R$, $r=r_X$, $s=r_Y$ and $\beta=d$. Steps 1 and 2 verify its ordinary counit equality, exactness, existence of resolutions, preservation of K-injectives, and normalization of $d$. Its identities are read through $u,c$ rather than as literal equalities of differently presented module objects. Exact-functor localization supplies their termwise derived identifications. It follows that
$$r_X(\varepsilon_{S,N})=\varepsilon_{R,r_XN}\circ L_R(d_N).$$
Consequently, for $t:L_SM\to N$, its $S$-adjunct $t^\sharp:M\to G_SN$ satisfies
$$\bigl(r_X(t)\circ u_M\bigr)^{\sharp_R}=d_N\circ r_Y(t^\sharp).$$
Indeed, inverse-transpose the right side by composing with $\varepsilon_R$: the counit identity above and naturality of $u$ give $r_X(\varepsilon_SN\circ L_S(t^\sharp))\circ u_M=r_X(t)\circ u_M$. This proves the asserted compatibility with adjoint transposes for the actual derived adjunctions.

proof.text:
Set $A=G_RK$, let $\chi:L_SE_Y\cong E_XL_R$ be the specified comparison, and put $B=G_R(\Phi_{X,K})\,d_{E_XK}\,r_Y(\gamma_K)\,\Phi_{Y,A}^{-1}$. The scalar-comparison normalization identifies $\chi$ with the ordinary balancing comparison on models, and the coordinate lemma gives its inverse-image compatibility and naturality. Explicitly, the $i$th input $m\mapsto b_i\otimes m$ is carried by $r_X(\chi)u$ to the same input for the pulled-back basis $h^{-1}b_i$; applying $r_X(E_X\varepsilon_{R,K})$ and then $\Phi_X$ puts $\varepsilon_{R,K}(m)$ in the $i$th summand. The coordinate lemma states these identities in the unbounded derived category as well. By step 3 and naturality of the Hom bijection, the $R$-transpose of $B\iota_i$ is therefore
$$\iota_i\varepsilon_{R,K}:L_RG_RK\longrightarrow K^{\oplus d}.$$
The transpose of $G_R(\iota_i)$ is the same map, by naturality of $\varepsilon_R$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection yields $B\iota_i=G_R(\iota_i)$. The finite coproduct universal property now gives $B=\sigma_K$, the claimed equality of specified maps.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback); coordinate computation with the derived normalizations of the cited lemmas

proof.text:
Since $G_R$ is a right adjoint, it preserves the finite product $K^{\oplus d}$ and the zero object. Thus the maps $G_R(p_j)$ are jointly monic, and $G_R$ sends zero maps to zero maps (factor a zero map through the zero object). Put $\tau=\sum_i\iota_iG_R(p_i)$. The biproduct relations give
$$\tau\sigma\iota_j=\sum_i\iota_iG_R(p_i\iota_j)=\iota_j,$$
so $\tau\sigma=1$ by the coproduct property. Likewise
$$G_R(p_j)\sigma\tau=\sum_iG_R(p_j\iota_i)G_R(p_i)=G_R(p_j),$$
so $\sigma\tau=1$ by the preserved product property. This proves the specified inverse formula without requiring preservation of infinite sums. For $d=0$ the coproduct and product are zero objects and the empty sum is their unique identity morphism; the same argument applies.

proof.text: Step 4 identifies $r_Y(\gamma_K)$, up to the isomorphisms $\Phi_X,\Phi_Y,d$, with the isomorphism $\sigma_K$ of step 5. Exact restriction is computed termwise on representatives by its localization comparison and commutes with cohomology: its preservation of kernels and cokernels identifies $H^n(r_Yf)$ with $r_YH^n(f)$ directly from the kernel/image formula. Ordinary restriction reflects isomorphisms: an inverse of a bijective $S_Y$-linear sheaf map is $S_Y$-linear because $f(sm)=sf(m)$. Hence $r_Y(\gamma_K)$ invertible implies every $H^n(\gamma_K)$ invertible. The unbounded cohomology criterion implies that $\gamma_K$ itself is invertible. Every construction above used small-site resolutions and the finite frame, with no bound on $K$ and no geometric assumption on $h$.
